review:
Ich empfehle es, aber werde nicht warm damit. 

Seit WoW Classic 2004 liebe ich MMOs und vor allem dieses. Mir fehlt nur aktuell die Zeit und die Lust für den Grind. Also dachte ich mir: Geil! Hier kannste dein eigenes bauen. Also fing ich an. Ich designte grob ein paar Areas, setzte Mobs, baute Stufengebiete bis LvL 5 aus, setzte meinen ersten Dungeon, aber alles in allem war meine Welt lieblos und scheiße - die Spieler kamen trotzdem. Mir ist die AI - Spielergemeinschaft einfach ein wenig zu anspruchslos. 

Natürlich könnte ich jetzt mehr Lvl designen, mit dem erwirtschafteten Geld die Areas liebevoller dekorieren und ein echt schönes Spiel bauen...aber mir fehlt dieser "Wozu" Moment in diesem Spiel. Ich frage mich eher "warum spiel ich das?" Es gab mir die ersten 2h alles und seitdem irgendwie nichts mehr. 

Man kann alles einstellen, Monster, Klassen, NPCs, Waffen freischalten, jeden Parameter setzen aber irgendwie ist es mir zu langweilig geworden weil halt selbst für ein Tycoon Spiel nichts passiert. Abgesehen davon finde ich die KI spieler nicht so Intelligent und man braucht in jedem Gebiet alles. Überall Lehrer, überall Händler. Sie gehen nicht zum lernen oder verkaufen in andere Gebiete, wie man es selbst als Spieler in MMOS machen muss. 

Alles in allem fühlt es sich trotz den ganzen möglichkeiten und der echt niedlichen Grafik einfach leer und tot an. 

Ich glaube für Spieler die alle 30 Min was machen wollen und ansonsten nebenher Arbeiten oder sonstwas machen ist es perfekt, aber zum permanent dran sitzen und zocken ist es mir einfach auch zu langsam.

The game has given me a lot of gameplay for a small price tag. This is one of those games I will be playing for years and has made it onto my Kerbal/Rimworld play cycle that I don't think I will ever put down.

- The characters/monsters are very fun to create and customize. 
- The overword is a little limited in shape and you can only choose from presets. However, the zones themselves allow for heavy customization.
- The classes and movesets are broad and enjoyable. There are still 'conditions' that I would like to see, such as temporary buffs to movement or attack speed.
- Dungeons are cool! Boss 'phases' make for really interesting to watch fights.
- Love seeing my players maneuver through the world by boat, airship, portal.
- Excited to see future content and each update is a joy to see what it brings. Often a lot of awesome thematic cosmetics.
- Though I love designing quests, I would love to have 'special quest chain' events that allow for a longer quest chain that rewards my NPCs with a special choice of loot. That would incentivise my NPCs to do the chain which would then encourage them to go to certain locations in a particular order.
- Wish down the road there was some ability to allow for friends to play in your world as a NPC. However, the road map has an excellent list of upcoming features.

Story -/10 - Make your own!
Graphics 7/10 - Sticks close to its own visual theme. It can look gorgeous if you make it so!
Sound 6/10 - Music is great but we need more options. Also I would love to have more customization in the moves to allow for specific sounds.
Gameplay 8/10 - Customization is huge, and with a little more additions here and there it will be great! I find the game loop really enjoyable, and creating a world for my little NPC's to play is awesome. 
Technical Performance 9/10 - The game runs well (for me), few present bugs. 


- With continued development I think this might be one of my favourite management games ever.

I booted up MMO RPG Tycoon 2 thinking I’d casually build a cute little fantasy world.

3 hours later I was manually adjusting EXP curves because “Level 7 felt emotionally incorrect.”

10 hours later I had:

A fully functioning economy
A forest that taxes players for breathing
And a dungeon boss I nerfed 6 times because he kept committing mass player genocide

At some point I realized… I’m not playing an MMO.

I AM the unpaid developer.

You don’t just design quests—you question your own morality:
“Should wolves drop pants?”
“Is it ethical to make players walk this far?”
“Do I hate fun?”

Also, nothing humbles you faster than watching your “perfectly balanced game” get absolutely destroyed by NPCs named stuff like Greg the Slightly Damp.

Performance: My PC is fine. My sanity is not.
Gameplay: Addictive. Dangerous. Spreadsheet simulator disguised as a game.
Difficulty: Depends how much you respect your own time (I clearly don’t).

10/10 would accidentally become a game designer again.

MMORPG Tycoon 2 is a sequel to MMORPG Tycoon, which was a very simplistic game where you created a mmorpg for virtual players to play. This game contains better gameplay and more visuals compared to the original one, which might be interesting to look at if you want a mmorpg game simulation.

Here you can create a custom mmorpg game, with its own name, thematic and everything else. The world map is generated via chunks, which you can keep clicking to regenerate until it creates lands in a way you like (You can also terraform underwater or overwater lands to be places the player can/can't go).

You can create custom classes, monsters and npcs for the game, and make use of a quite powerful character creator to create any kind of character you want to fill those roles. You can for example make a game with classic rpg characters, like the warrior, mage and stuff; or you can make a it just be a bunch of of differently colored bunnies.

The characters can be setup easily by sliders on how much health, mana and rage they can have, aswell as their skill sets can be fully customized, from effects to their potence, resource costs and stuff. You can even make aoe skills too.

You can setup zones with their own level range, and place structures, roads and even monsters to spawn in them. Structures can be functional, like an INN for adventurers to logout at, tavern so they can gather and make parties (when unlocked) and stuff, blacksmith to buy equipments and more.

The game you make in the mmorpg tycoon is in constant development, being that you need to earn funding through having players buy and play the game, in order to develop more features for the game, like unlocking parties, friends list, dungeons and etc. And I gotta tell you, that unlocking the new features is really cool, and the fact you can actually design the dungeons and their bosses is badass too.

Relying on monthly payment and players buying the game is extremely unreliable, and takes way too long, since the game time passes way too slow even on 3x speed, so eventually making the game pay to win ends up being a meta. Like, having some INNs the player can use if they use real money, or blacksmith shop you can buy gear from with money and etc.

The downside right now about the game, is that the game isn't very reliable as a idle game, since it tends to crash to desktop when you leave it running, so you might leave the game running while you do something else, and when you return, you discover the game is gone.

The other downside is that the party system dumbfies the characters in them, making them waste time running the whole region trying to look for mobs to kill, wasting time they could use to progress in the game.

The game itself has 20 levels you can create contents to, and to help you get more players into it, you can buy advertisements too. There's even streamers that can help with popularity, but sadly, they only show up after a major update is launched (You need about $50k to launch a major update in the game).

Anyways, this simulator is pretty cool to play around, and watching the players running around doing their stuff is fun too. Even more when you make a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ difficulty game, and lock the graveyard behind a paywall, then you see that mass of ghosts flying back to their doom.
